Recorded claim:
Entry299 allowed a specific directly nested encryption layer below an outer S/MIME signature but ignored that outer signature for author identity; inner signed content can still be authenticated. It kept negative cases where an unrelated multipart layer intervenes. Current classifier has newer explicit parent-object and depth checks plus more CMS cases, so do not copy the old ignoredLayer implementation as current architecture. Any change to admitted MIME nesting needs positive and negative fixtures and must preserve the protection against decrypted hidden content leaking into reply or forward. No cryptographic runtime validation was done here.
